BXL-00019-v1.headline: Parliament backs new Brussels government in confidence vote
BXL-00019-v1.source_brief: After more than 600 days without a formed regional government following the June 2024 election, the new Brussels government sought Parliament's confidence at the close of its policy declaration of 23 February 2026. The motion of confidence was approved by 51 votes to 27. The seven majority parties (PS, MR, Open VLD, Les Engagés, Groen, CD&V, Vooruit) voted in favour, while the opposition (PTB, DéFI, Team Fouad Ahidar, Vlaams Belang, Ecolo, N-VA) voted against, criticising the declaration as vague and the budget as not yet voted.
BXL-00019-v1.stake: Whether to invest the new government and end the longest government-formation deadlock in the Region's history.

BXL-00020-A-215.headline: Resolution urges immediate ceasefire and aid in Darfur and Sudan
BXL-00020-A-215.source_brief: The resolution (A-215) calls for an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Darfur and Sudan and for the strengthening and securing of humanitarian aid and support arrangements. It was adopted with 72 votes in favour and 3 abstentions; the Open VLD (Anders.) group abstained while nearly all other members voted for it. Sponsors described it as a strong cross-party signal on an often-overlooked humanitarian crisis.
BXL-00020-A-215.stake: Whether the Brussels Parliament should formally call for a ceasefire and expanded humanitarian access in Sudan.

BXL-00021-A-264.headline: Brussels approves polluter-pays deal making producers fund litter cleanup
BXL-00021-A-264.source_brief: This ordinance gives assent to an interregional cooperation agreement of 9 February 2026 on Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for certain waste streams and litter. Applying the polluter-pays principle, producers of packaging, tobacco products, wipes and similar items would fund the management of the resulting waste and the related public-cleanliness costs, expected to bring the Region around 50 million euros a year, with 54% of the litter share going to municipalities. It was approved by a large majority; PTB and Team Fouad Ahidar abstained, citing concerns that costs could be passed on to households.
BXL-00021-A-264.stake: Whether to require producers, rather than the public, to pay for cleaning up the litter their products generate.
